gh_b256c39c80fcfe7ea8df79e4.title: Add a UKG Pro Recruiting (UltiPro) source adapter (19 verified job boards)
gh_b256c39c80fcfe7ea8df79e4.description:
## Problem

**UKG Pro Recruiting** (UltiPro) has 21 employers on the 30-day applied-jobs export (#390), more than any other job system still unsupported except iCIMS (backlog in #316). None of their postings reach the board.

## Evidence (probed 2026-10-14)

- **The public job-board search needs no key.** `POST https://<host>/<tenant>/JobBoard/<board-id>/JobBoardView/LoadSearchResults` with `{"opportunitySearch": {"Top": N, "Skip": M, "OrderBy": [postedDateDesc], "Filters": []}}` returns `opportunities` and `totalCount`.
- **All 19 boards in the export answer HTTP 200 with postings,** from the Cleveland Guardians (4) to Gray Media (504). The hosts are `recruiting.ultipro.com`, `recruiting2.ultipro.com` and `<company>.rec.pro.ukg.net`. Results sort newest first and pages don't overlap. `Top` accepts at least 500.
- **Each opportunity has** `Id`, `Title`, `PostedDate`, a `BriefDescription`, and `Locations` with a structured `Address` (city, state code, country). `LocalizedName` is often null, so the location must be built from the address. `JobLocationType` (null/0/1/2) does not reliably mark remote work: a "Remote / Virtual" posting has none, so the adapter doesn't use it.
- **The posting page `<board>/OpportunityDetail?opportunityId=<Id>` answers 200.**
- **Many tenants share `recruiting.ultipro.com`,** so the 403 cooldown must key on the tenant path, not the host.

## Proposed solution

1. Let `ngj.http.fetch_json_with_retry` take an optional JSON body, which sends a POST with the same cooldown and error handling. POST is not retried at the transport level, which is correct. Timeouts still get the board-level retry pass.
2. Add `scripts/ngj/sources/ukg.py`, returning `SourceResult`. It pages the search newest first, caps each board, builds locations from the address, skips postings without an `Id`, and returns no partial jobs on a timeout or network error.
3. Register UKG as a board source (`apis.ukg.companies: [{name, url}]`, where `url` is the job-board URL). That covers the registry, pipeline, `Settings`, `validate_config.py`, tenant-level cooldown keys, README sync and the site's source label. Add the 19 verified boards.
4. Test with mocked HTTP only, then run a real local scrape and `check_integrity.py` before the PR.

## Also probed (not in this issue)

- **ADP Workforce Now** (`careercenter/public/events/staffing/v1/job-requisitions?cid=…`): public JSON for the 3 employers on it. A small follow-up.
- **ADP MyJobs** (10 employers): answers `400 Missing orgoid header`. Not keyless as it stands.
- **Paylocity** (16): the export's links carry no company ID, and the ID found on one posting page returned an empty feed. Needs more digging.

gh_b29f7d5bd90361353b30b563.title: [Advanced]: add iCIMS ingestion support to recover enterprise networking and infrastructure coverage
gh_b29f7d5bd90361353b30b563.description:
### 🧠 Advanced Contributors
This issue is for contributors who are already very familiar with this codebase
and its architectural patterns.

You should feel comfortable:
- Understanding the full data flow: `config.yml` → fetch → filter → dedup → categorize → commit
- Reading and modifying `ThreadPoolExecutor` logic and thread-safety considerations
- Reasoning about API contract changes across ATS providers
- Writing rigorous, deterministic tests without live network calls

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **You must be assigned before starting** — comment `/assign` to claim this issue.
> PRs submitted without a prior assignment will be closed.

### 🐞 Problem Description
The roadmap already calls out ATS coverage expansion as the biggest remaining quality gap. Today, the scraper has strong coverage for Greenhouse, Lever, Google Careers, and partial Workday, but it still misses entire slices of enterprise hiring that sit behind other ATS platforms.

iCIMS is a high-leverage next source because it is common among larger employers, including companies that post entry-level infrastructure, networking, and security roles that never reach the board today.

Without a first-class iCIMS integration, the dataset will continue to under-represent one of the main role families the README says it tracks.

### 💡 Proposed / Expected Solution
Add a production-ready iCIMS fetch path that follows the same project constraints as the existing sources:

- config-driven company definitions
- deterministic tests with mocked responses
- compatibility with the current normalization, filtering, and dedup pipeline
- no external database or browser-based dependency

This should be implemented as a source integration, not as a one-off company patch.

### ✅ Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A reusable iCIMS fetch path exists in the scraper
- [ ] `config.yml` can declare iCIMS-backed companies without custom code per company
- [ ] New source behavior is covered by deterministic tests with mocked payloads
- [ ] Thread-safety is preserved
- [ ] All existing `pytest tests/` pass
- [ ] New tests added for every changed code path (deterministic — no live network calls)
- [ ] `pre-commit run --all-files` passes
- [ ] `jobs.json` schema remains backward compatible with `docs/app.js`
- [ ] PR is linked to this issue with `Fixes #<number>`
- [ ] PR title follows Conventional Commits format

### 🏗️ Which area does this touch?
🤖 Core scraper (scripts/update_jobs.py)

### 🔗 Additional Context
- Roadmap reference: `ROADMAP.md` lists iCIMS support under v1.1
- Existing ATS references: Greenhouse, Lever, Google Careers, Workday

gh_b25d50b22a63ca6c3f5b072d.description:
## Descrição da vaga

Se você busca atuar em produtos que impactam a vida das pessoas, e cujo propósito é auxiliar a salvar vidas, temos uma vaga que pode ser do seu interesse.

Buscamos front end developer que ame reproduzir protótipos de alta fidelidade em código, que pense fora da caixa e preze pela experiência do usuário. Aqui valorizamos a colaboração e a participação nos processos de desenvolvimento, com questionamentos e sugestões de melhorias.

## Local

Anywhere office

## Benefícios

- Descanso remunerado;
- Bonificação anual; 
- Anywhere office; 
- Laura Care; 
- Gympass; 
- Auxílio remoto - Cartão Caju; 
- Auxílio alimentação/refeição - Cartão Caju.

#### Diferenciais

- Oportunidade de trabalhar em uma das 100 startups to watch do Brasil, com crescimento de 250% no último ano; 
- Vivência com um time multidisciplinar: profissionais da área da saúde, engenharia, tecnologia, inovação e muito mais; 
- Trabalhar em um local que valoriza a discussão em grupo, troca e compartilhamento de informações;
- Ambiente de aprendizado e desenvolvimento contínuo, com flexibilidade e pessoas incríveis.
## Requisitos

**Obrigatórios:**
- ECMAScript 6 ou superior
- Sólida experiência em React e seu ecossistema (hooks, redux, styled components, etc)
- Domínio de HTML e CSS
- Padrões de API (RESTful ou GraphQL)
- Experiência com controle de versão (Git, Mercurial, etc)
- Experiência com serviços em nuvem (Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, etc)
- Experiência com ferramentas de CI/CD (Github Actions, CodeCircle, etc)
- Docker

**Desejáveis:**
- Animações CSS e JS
- TypeScript
- Experiência com alguma biblioteca UI (material-ui, bootstrap, tailwind)
- Ferramentas de código (Eslint, Husky, Prettier, Webpack, Babel, etc)
- Websockets

## Contratação

PJ a combinar

## Nossa empresa

Nosso objetivo é democratizar o acesso à saúde através da tecnologia para ajudar a salvar vidas. 🧡

Em maio de 2010, após perder sua filha para uma doença chamada SEPSE, foi que Jac Fressatto criou a Robô Laura. Através do uso da nossa tecnologia, ajudamos entidades a tomarem decisões mais assertivas, salvar vidas e gerar economia de custos. A Robô Laura já ajuda a salvar pelo menos 18 vidas por dia e já passamos a marca de 8 milhões de atendimentos realizados.

## Como se candidatar

Por favor, envie um email para camila.souza@laura-br.com com link do LinkedIn ou currículo e telefone para contato, assunto: Front-end Developer

## Labels

- 🏢 Flexível
- 🏢 Remoto
- 👴 Sênior
- ⚖️ PJ
- 💰 5k-10k
